title: A Customer's Worth: CLV Explained Simply | Marketing Management Ep 34
description:
Mrs. Rao pays Rs 120 for a Laddoo Lab 6-pack, so Arjun calls her a Rs 120 customer. Zoya disagrees: Mrs. Rao buys every school week, year after year. In this animated lesson we work out what one loyal customer is really worth.

You will see what customer lifetime value (CLV) means, the simple formula (profit per year, times the years a customer stays, minus the cost to win them) and a full worked example with example figures: Rs 40 profit per pack, 40 school weeks, Rs 1,600 a year, Rs 8,000 over five years, about Rs 6,065 in today's money at 10% a year, and Rs 5,565 after the Rs 500 it cost to win her. Then we pull the four levers of CLV, with workplace examples from a phone maker, a coffee shop, a gym and a bank. We also look at the human side honestly: Werner Reinartz and V. Kumar (Harvard Business Review, 2002) found that loyal customers are not always the most profitable, and CLV should guide where you invest, not whom you respect.

This is Episode 34 of our Marketing Management series for MBA, BBA and commerce students.
